newsitem.title: CANADA: Tee-Com seen close to finding U.S. partner.
newsitem.headline: Tee-Com seen close to finding U.S. partner.

text.p: Tee-Com Electronics Inc could be close to lining up a strategic partner to help underwrite its push into the competitive U.S. home satellite television market, analysts said on Tuesday.

Tee-Com shares, which fell on profit-taking in Toronto Stock Exchange trading on Tuesday, have risen recently amid rumors the company was in partnership talks with such companies as US West Inc, Sprint Corp and Excel Communications Inc.
"There is a lot of speculation and rumor that a deal is much closer than in the past," said analyst Vince Valentini at Midland Walwyn.
Tee-Com was off 0.20 to 13.75 on Tuesday after rising by 1.90 in heavy trading on Monday. The stock has risen steadily in the past few weeks from a low of 9.10 on August 20.
Tee-Com, a maker of satellite television equipment, became the fourth company to enter the booming U.S. satellite television market when it launched its AlphaStar Television Network in July.
Analysts said the company needed either marketing muscle from a big U.S. company or an equity stake so it can go head to head in the market that has been marked by sharp discounting in recent weeks.
Tee-Com has announced that it hired Toronto brokerage Nesbitt Burns to help it seek a partner for its 97 percent- owned Alpha Star.
"They are certainly dealing in a market that's become quite competitive and they are dealing with competitors who have much deeper pockets than them," said analyst Valentini.
It has been estimated that some five million households or six percent of the U.S. market have signed up for satellite TV.
Otis Bradley, an analyst at Gilford Securities in New York, believes the U.S. market has nowhere to go but up and predicted the subscriber base would reach 40 milllion households by the year 2000.

Bradley said it was imperative that Tee-Com line up a partner if it hoped to be a significant player in the market. "It requires a lot of money and lot of marketing muscle and Tee-Com needs a partner."
Meanwhile, Tee-Com said on Tuesday it was cutting the price of its satellite dishes to US$399, but said that its offer did not come with the conditions attached by its competitors.
